csv_scope_of_work: The Geotechnical Engineering Services work may include, but is not limited to: subsurface exploration, in-situ testing, geophysical methods, geotechnical instrumentation, laboratory testing, geotechnical analysis, and providing recommendations using the latest AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, MDOT s Bridge Design Manual, and MDOT s Geotechnical Manual. Additionally, required services may include Standard Penetration Test (SPT), undisturbed soil sampling, rock coring and the ability to perform standard geotechnical field and laboratory testing (gradation analysis, classification, shear strength, consolidation testing, vane shear testing, water level monitoring, etc.).
csv_disciplines_requested: Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Structural Engineering, Traffic Design Engineering

title: As-Needed Geotechnical Engineering Services
short_description: On-call geotechnical services for MDOT highway and bridge-related investigations and recommendations.
project_scope: As-needed geotechnical engineering services for streets/highways projects, potentially including bridge-related work. Scope may include subsurface exploration, in-situ testing, geophysical methods, geotechnical instrumentation, laboratory testing, geotechnical analysis, and recommendations based on AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, the MDOT Bridge Design Manual, and the MDOT Geotechnical Manual. Specific tasks may include Standard Penetration Tests, undisturbed soil sampling, rock coring, gradation analysis, soil classification, shear strength testing, consolidation testing, vane shear testing, and water level monitoring. Up to 3 contracts may be awarded under an as-needed arrangement.
services: Geotechnical engineering services; subsurface investigation; field and laboratory testing; geotechnical analysis; bridge/highway-related recommendations. Disciplines requested: civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, structural engineering, traffic design engineering.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily an as-needed geotechnical services contract, which is outside sbp's core focus.
- No defined bridge, building, roof, stadium, or special structure project is identified.
- Scope is dominated by soil investigation, testing, and geotechnical recommendations.
- Although bridge design specifications are referenced, no structural design scope or specific structure is tendered.
- Framework-style/on-call procurement with broad scope and no technical structural definition is of low strategic relevance for sbp.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction cost is stated. This is an on-call professional services procurement for geotechnical engineering, not a defined construction project. No project size, quantities, or budget information is provided that would support a realistic construction cost estimate.
fee_explanation: No fee information is stated. The notice describes an as-needed services contract with a 36-month base period and 24-month renewal option, and up to 3 contracts may be awarded, but no contract value or fee budget is provided.
references_qualifications: Bidders must be capable of providing geotechnical engineering services including subsurface exploration, in-situ testing, geophysical methods, instrumentation, laboratory testing, geotechnical analysis, SPT, undisturbed sampling, rock coring, and standard geotechnical field and laboratory testing in accordance with AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications and MDOT manuals.
contracting_authority: Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT), Lansing, Michigan, USA. Contact: Erron J. Peuse. Email: peusee@michigan.gov. Phone: 517-242-3369. Website: https://mdotjboss4.state.mi.us/eprop/saml/requestsForProposals.htm
notes: Project number 4606. Target market: Streets/Highways. Funding: federal and state. Stage: RFP/RFQ. Contract duration: 36-month base period with 24-month renewal option; renewable. Up to 3 contracts may be awarded. Despite references to bridge design standards, this is not a defined bridge design tender but an on-call geotechnical services procurement.
